q: The paper attributes teleportation fidelity loss to a mixture of multiphoton events, residual polarization distinguishability at the BSM, and fiber dephasing, but does not publish the per-mechanism fractional contribution to 1 - F_avg. Our pure-dephasing sweep hits F=0.89 at lambda_pd ~ 0.24; injecting depolarizing noise would push that up. What is the quantitatively resolved error budget per mechanism?
basis: In our qiskit-aer sweep a single phase-damping channel reproduces the reported F=0.89 exactly, but the paper explicitly lists three distinct physical error sources. The paper's own model would predict a different lambda_pd if run in isolation.
next_steps: Fit a joint amplitude-damping + phase-damping + depolarizing noise model to the paper's per-state QST fidelities (Table in paper Sec. III) and solve for the three coefficients simultaneously; publish the resulting error budget.

q: The paper reports QST-averaged fidelity across a specific finite tomography basis. Our statevector reproduction is F=1 for every input state including 4 Haar-random ones. Would a truly Haar-averaged fidelity on the real hardware yield the same 89%, or would non-Clifford states expose lower fidelity from state-dependent BSM inefficiency?
basis: We ran an explicit Haar-random-state bank (theta,phi uniform) in the ideal sim and got F=1.000000000000. The paper only averages over a limited set. State-dependent hardware artifacts (e.g. HOM-visibility asymmetry) would show up on Haar-random inputs but not on the paper's basis.
next_steps: Prepare a suite of ~30 Haar-random time-bin qubits on FQNET/CQNET, run QST, and check whether F_avg over the extended set is statistically consistent with the reported 0.89.

q: The paper finds no significant fidelity degradation between back-to-back and +22 km fiber configurations (both F_avg = 0.89 +/- 0.01). In our simulation this would require the effective dephasing lambda_pd to be fiber-length independent over that range, which is unusual for real telecom fiber. What physical mechanism saturates the channel dephasing at short length?
basis: Our noise sweep shows F is monotonically decreasing with lambda_pd, so equal experimental F with and without 22 km fiber implies lambda_pd(0km) ~ lambda_pd(22km). This is inconsistent with typical fiber-dephasing scaling; the dominant loss mechanism must live in the source/BSM, not the fiber.
next_steps: Repeat the experiment at 44 km and 66 km fiber and check whether the fidelity finally rolls off; if not, the paper's ~0.89 ceiling is source-limited and increasing brightness/detector efficiency rather than shortening fiber is the correct improvement axis.

q: Our reproduction defers Bob's classical corrections through if-test contexts and assumes a perfect classical channel. On real hardware the Charlie->Bob classical link has finite latency and finite bit-error rate. What is the teleportation fidelity's sensitivity to a symmetric bit-flip on the 2-bit BSM announcement, and does the paper's +/- 1% error bar already contain that budget?
basis: In our sim, corrupting one bit of the BSM outcome converts (X,Z) into (Y,I) etc., degrading F by ~2*(1-p_correct) for a Pauli-flip on one axis. The paper does not quantify classical-channel noise contribution.
next_steps: Extend teleport_sim.py to include a Bernoulli bit-flip model on the classical channel and re-sweep; compare degradation slope to the paper's stated error bar.

q: The paper's Bell-state fidelity F_ent = 97.3% strictly upper-bounds F_avg via well-known inequalities. Our statevector reproduction has F_ent = 1 exactly, so F_avg = 1 too. Working backwards on hardware: what joint noise model simultaneously reproduces BOTH F_ent = 0.973 AND F_avg = 0.89? A single dephasing channel doesn't -- the two fidelities constrain different degrees of freedom.
basis: F_ent and F_avg gap in the paper (97.3% vs 89%) is much larger than a single-channel dephasing model can explain. Our sweep confirms: matching F_avg=0.89 with only phase damping forces F_ent << 0.973.
next_steps: Solve for a two-parameter model (dephasing at Bob's Bell-pair generation + additional depolarization at the BSM interference) that simultaneously fits both numbers; verify by ranging over multiphoton mean-photon-number parameters mu_A.
